name: verbal-relay-provenance-convention
claim: When the operator relays a verbal or informal external communication (a text message, phone call, in-person conversation) that causes a field to be written, the provenance entry uses source user:<operator>:<date> (the existing authorship prefix from b030) and the verbatim quote or paraphrase is recorded in the note field. No new source type is introduced. If the communication is later confirmed by a cached artifact (email thread, calendar event), a follow-up provenance entry cites that artifact and notes that it corroborates the prior attestation.

evidence.detail: The user asked whether verbal relays need a distinct provenance category. An audit of existing entries confirmed the user-handle-and-date pattern with a free-text note is already the established convention. Formalizing it avoids inventing a parallel source type.
